documents.body: NATO has formally approved a landmark procurement agreement for a new generation of medium-range air-defence missiles, involving Germany, Poland, and the Baltic states. The deal, valued at approximately €2.5 billion, aims to bolster air defenses against evolving threats across the alliance’s eastern flank. Initial missile deliveries are slated to commence in spring 2025, with full operational capability expected within two years. The agreement underscores a commitment to collective security and enhanced interoperability among member nations.

documents.body: EU foreign ministers convened in Brussels today to finalize a new package of sanctions targeting officials and entities linked to the government of Eldoria. The sanctions are expected to be formally adopted and published later this week.

documents.body: Wildfires fueled by strong winds and high temperatures are rapidly spreading across the Peloponnese and Crete regions of southern Greece. Authorities have ordered the evacuation of the coastal villages of Monemvasia, Areopoli, and Palaia Epidavros as flames encroach on populated areas. Greece has formally requested assistance from the European Union's civil protection mechanism, seeking additional firefighting resources. Several hundred firefighters are currently battling the blazes, with aerial support hampered by challenging wind conditions.

The victory secures her Diamond League title and cements her place among the sport’s all-time greats.

EuroChip estimates the plant will create over 1,500 high-skilled jobs.

documents.body: European regulators have granted approval for Cablivi, a novel long-acting injectable medication designed to prevent HIV infection. The treatment, administered every eight weeks, offers a significant alternative to daily oral PrEP regimens. Rollout across European Union member states is anticipated to begin by mid-year, pending national implementation plans. Health officials believe Cablivi could substantially reduce new HIV cases and improve adherence rates.

documents.title: Lost Poems of Polish Romantic Found in Vienna Archives
documents.body: A previously unknown manuscript containing dozens of poems by a prominent 19th-century Polish poet has been unearthed in the Austrian National Library’s vast archives. The collection, believed to have been smuggled out of Poland during a period of political upheaval, offers fresh insights into the poet's early development and Romantic influences. Experts are hailing the discovery as a significant contribution to Polish literary history, promising new avenues for scholarly research. Initial assessments suggest the poems explore themes of national identity, exile, and longing.
